text.en: Yoga Sadhana is regular practice. We start with preparatory practices that warm up the body and then learn asanas to build strength and flexibility.

Preparatory practices warm up the body before asanas.
Asanas in the book include Padmasana, Dandasana, Janu Sirsasana, Vrikshasana, Trikonasana, Pada Hastasana, Ustrasana, Shashankasana, Sarvangasana and Parvatasana. Each is practised with its preparatory practices and a complementary posture.
Pranayama calms the mind. We revise Anuloma Viloma pranayama, breathing in and out through alternate nostrils.
Mudras improve focus. In Chin Mudra the hand rests on the knee with a special finger position.
Bindu Trataka is a cleansing practice (kriya) of gazing at a point without blinking.
Krida Yoga includes group yoga games such as Matsya Kridasana, to learn group coordination.
End practice with relaxation in Shavasana. Practise slowly, carefully and under your teacher's guidance.

problem.en: Why do we do Shavasana at the end?

text.en: It is the usual finish for yoga practice.
